affiliations.role_title: Draftee assigned to the Engineer Corps

affiliations.research_notes: A direct 1992 interview says Moon was transferred from the Engineer Corps to OSS. This is a military assignment, not a civilian employer. The Army bulk record independently dates his entry into military service but its coded occupation was not used.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Thomas N. Moon is a high-confidence match to the Army enlistee and OSS Detachment 101 member documented as T/5 Tom Moon.
claims.evidence_excerpt: T/5 Thomas N. Moon, and agent “King” somewhere in Burma, early 1944.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Two official records agree in exact name and a nonshared protected identifier; official Army history then gives the full name, rank, KNOTHEAD unit, and photograph.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence because exact full name, nonshared protected identifier, T/5 rank, Detachment 101 assignment, and direct retrospective account form a consistent identity chain.
claims.temporal_assessment: The evidence identifies the same soldier before and during OSS service; it does not establish his civilian pre-service employer.
claims.match_notes: The index prints T-3 while official Army history documents T/5 in early 1944; rank change is plausible but is not silently reconciled. Box 534 remains the direct file pointer.

claims.claim_text: Thomas N. Moon's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the U.S. Army Engineer Corps in Louisiana.
claims.evidence_excerpt: plucked out of the Engineer Corps in Louisiana and transferred to the OSS
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A direct interview explicitly describes Moon's transfer from the Engineer Corps to OSS; the official Army enlistment record corroborates his military status and entry date.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The direct interview's name, Nebraska origin, age, Detachment 101 service, and authorship agree with the official identity chain.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate predecessor: the source directly states that Moon moved from the Engineer Corps to OSS.
claims.match_notes: This is published as a military assignment, not as an employer or last civilian employer. No civilian pre-service employer was found.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The index and official Army bulk record agree in exact full name and a nonshared protected identifier; official Army history gives T/5 Thomas N. Moon in KNOTHEAD, and a direct interview documents his Engineer Corps-to-OSS transfer.
person_updates.next_action: Inspect the Box 534 personnel file and CSUF oral history OH 2395 for Moon's last civilian employer before his January 1943 Army entry and for exact assignment dates.

research_attempts.query_text: Thomas N Moon; Tom Moon; T/5; T-3; OSS; Detachment 101; KNOTHEAD; Engineer Corps; employer; occupation
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: The LoC candidate was an unrelated radio listing; generic directory and people-finder namesakes lacked OSS, rank, protected-identifier, or archival bridges; postwar writing and insurance work were not back-projected.
research_attempts.research_notes: The CIA adapter failed closed when robots policy could not be retrieved and was not treated as negative evidence. A targeted public CIA-domain review located official Detachment 101 bibliographic context. The direct interview explicitly supports the Engineer Corps as the immediate military assignment; no last civilian employer was identified.
research_attempts.next_action: Inspect Box 534 and CSUF OH 2395 for the last civilian employer and exact transfer chronology.
